ops.title: ccx vcs ship reports 'pushed <branch> -> origin' on the jj lane even when jj pushed elsewhere
ops.description:
`internal/cli/ship.go:1016` — `shipPushJJ` returns the literal string `"origin"`
as the remote it pushed to, so the ship summary always reads
`· pushed <branch> → origin` regardless of where jj actually pushed.

Reproduced on a real repository (2026-08-03): with `git.push = backup` set in jj
config and an untracked counterpart bookmark on BOTH remotes, ship tracks
`backup`, jj pushes to `backup`, and the summary still says `origin`. Confirmed
by state, not prose — a first draft of the test asserted the commit was on origin
and failed with `origin main = e134af87..., want the shipped commit 9a75723d...`.
The commit is only in `backup`'s store.

The hand-modeled fake could not disagree: it had no notion of where a push
landed, so the report was unfalsifiable. Found by
`TestShipJJRebase/multiple_untracked_counterparts_track_the_push_target`, which
now pins BOTH halves — the wrong summary and the right store — so the current
behavior is documented rather than silently accepted.

Fix: have `shipPushJJ` return the remote it resolved. `jjPushRemote` is already
read on the tie path, so the value is in hand.

The test should be flipped to assert the correct remote once fixed.

ops.text: The jj-lane ship summary names the remote the commit actually went to, matching what jj pushed
A test with git.push set to a non-origin remote asserts the summary names that remote, and fails if origin is hardcoded
